gold: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with IgA Nephropathy and Acute Progressive Glomerulonephritis
e7_s4_rationale: The patient has a positive ANA, Anti-SM, and U1-NRNP, which are specific autoantibodies associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The presence of low complement levels (C3 and C4) and the kidney biopsy findings of cellular crescents and IgA deposition also support this diagnosis.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis
e7_s4_rejected.why: While the patient has rapidly progressive renal failure, the presence of specific autoantibodies and low complement levels points more towards an immune-mediated disease like lupus nephritis

e7_s4_rejected.label: IgA nephropathy
e7_s4_rejected.why: Although the biopsy shows IgA deposition, the clinical presentation and other laboratory findings (e.g., positive ANA, Anti-SM, and U1-NRNP) are more consistent with lupus nephritis

e7_s4_rejected.label: Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease
e7_s4_rejected.why: There is no mention of anti-GBM antibodies, which are characteristic of this disease

e7_s4_rejected.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis
e7_s4_rejected.why: There is no mention of ANCA positivity or other typical features of vasculitis, such as granulomatosis or eosinophilia

B07_pred: IgA Nephropathy with Rapidly Progressive Glomerulonephritis (RPGN); Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with Renal Involvement
